fried: Air-fry, bake or shallow-fry with 1 tsp oil instead of deep-frying.
Blot fried food on paper towels and avoid re-using frying oil.
butter: Swap butter/ghee for 1 tsp cold-pressed oil (groundnut, sesame or olive) per serving.
cream: Replace cream with thick curd or blended cashew/onion paste; add it off the heat to avoid curdling.
refined_carb: Use whole-wheat, millet (ragi, jowar, bajra) or brown-rice versions.
Add vegetables, dal or sprouts to the same dish to lower its glycaemic load.
high_sugar: Reduce sugar by half, or sweeten with fruit or dates in small amounts.
high_fat: Trim visible fat, use less oil and thicken gravies with tomato, onion or dal instead of cream.
processed: Cook from scratch and season with herbs, lemon, ginger, garlic and spices instead of salt or sauces.
red_meat: Choose skinless chicken or fish, and grill or steam instead of frying.

plain_rice: Wash rice well, cook with extra water and drain; cooling then reheating raises resistant starch.
Keep the rice portion to about a quarter of the plate and fill the rest with vegetables and dal.
sambar: Load it with vegetables and use less tamarind and salt.
idli: Pair with sambar or a protein side (sprouts, egg) and use a little less rice in the batter, more urad dal.
masala_dosa: Use a non-stick pan with a drop of oil, and a thinner dosa with a vegetable-rich filling.
biryani: Use brown or parboiled rice, more vegetables and lean chicken; serve with raita and salad.

diabetes: Add a salad or dal first, then carbohydrates, to slow glucose rise.
hypertension: Cut added salt by a third; use lemon, coriander and spices for flavour.
obesity: Use smaller plates and cook with measured oil (1 tsp per person).
heart_disease: Prefer steaming, grilling, pressure-cooking and roasting.
kidney_disease: Leaching (soaking and boiling) vegetables in plenty of water lowers their potassium - ask your renal dietitian.
pcos: Combine carbohydrates with protein (dal, paneer, egg, sprouts) in every meal.
